historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (9.9% / 11.4%) is not usable as the growth anchor: book equity is a small residual after years of buybacks (2.0bn-2.7bn against ~37bn of market value) and diverges >30% from revenue and EPS. All 5-year figures start from the COVID-depressed FY2021 base and overstate trend. Organic growth is anchored on the 3-year revenue CAGR and FY2027 volume guidance (~2.5% local case growth plus 1-1.5% inflation).
historical_growth.notes: Annual (FY) rows only; quarterly Q4 rows are flagged as possibly mislabelled and were not used. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (CSV free cash flow = OCF less gross capex, less SBC): FY2021 1,337, FY2023 1,979, FY2026 1,820. SBC is ~5-6% of FCF and growing roughly in line, so reported and owner-FCF CAGRs do not materially diverge. inputs.reported_fcf uses the company definition (OCF 2,638 - capex 700 + asset-sale proceeds 176 = 2,114), which is levered: it is after ~690m of cash interest.

scenario_narratives.base: JRD closes around mid-February 2027 after HSR clearance without material remedies. Sysco's legacy business grows roughly with the market: ~2.5% local case growth plus 1-1.5% inflation, in line with FY2027 guidance, and JRD keeps adding about five warehouses a year at a ~14% EBITDA margin. The $250m synergy target arrives over three years but is partly offset by the restructuring and integration spend that Sysco has booked as 'Certain Items' every year, so the combined pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 6.8% versus 6.7% pro forma today. Free cash flow goes to debt reduction; leverage falls from ~4.5x toward 2.75x by FY2029 and buybacks resume late. Terminal value is capped at 16x free cash flow.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cash-and-carry channel proves complementary rather than cannibalising: Sysco sells private-label and specialty product through 170 JRD warehouses, wins delivery business from JRD's 725,000 independent-restaurant members, and JRD's warehouse roll-out accelerates on Sysco's balance sheet. Because JRD earns ~14% EBITDA margins against Sysco's ~5%, faster JRD growth lifts the blended margin, synergies exceed $250m, and AI-driven cost savings stick. Organic growth runs 4.5% and the margin reaches 7.3%. Deleveraging completes ahead of the 24-month plan.
scenario_narratives.bear: Restaurant traffic keeps falling (it was down ~2% in Q1 FY2027), GLP-1 adoption and consumer strain hold case growth near zero, and sales grow only with inflation at ~2%. JRD's unusually high margin (12.9% operating margin in a low-margin industry) erodes under Sysco ownership as competitors target its members, HSR remedies or a delayed close cost a few months of ownership, and integration spend consumes the synergies. The blended margin stalls at 6.0%. With ~32bn of net debt, a modest shortfall in operating value falls almost entirely on the equity: this is the scenario where the 2.75x leverage target slips well beyond 24 months and the Baa2/BBB ratings (already on negative outlook / under review) are at risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sysco is valued as the combined Sysco + Jetro Restaurant Depot company it has already financed itself to become: reported-basis revenue with the acquisition step in FY2027-28, a component-built unlevered owner FCF, and the full closing outflow (~21.9bn) deducted in the equity bridge against a 585m pro forma share count. The business is a stable, low-margin, high-turn distributor; the equity is now a levered claim on it, so small changes in the mature margin or the terminal multiple move per-share value disproportionately. SBC is immaterial (0.14% of sales), so the house and street bases are within a few dollars and the band carries little information.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage amplification: ~32.6bn of effective net debt against ~75bn of base-case enterprise value means a 10% change in EV moves equity value by roughly 18%
JRD margin durability: ~14% EBITDA margin on ~16bn of sales supplies about a third of combined EBITDA; a 2pt decline is worth ~0.3pt of blended margin

Deal timing and antitrust: every month of delay removes ~125m of JRD free cash flow while the acquisition notes accrue; a blocked deal triggers a 1.164bn termination fee and note redemption at 101, a branch this model does not value
Terminal multiple: the 14x/16x/18x cap binds in all three scenarios, so terminal growth has no effect on value at these settings and the cap is the live assumption
Recurring 'Certain Items': the margin path assumes ~0.15pt of sales of restructuring cost persists; if integration costs run higher or longer the base case is overstated
JRD figures come from one 8-K's audited and pro forma statements and have no reporting history under Sysco's controls or segment disclosure

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 68.19-91.85
data_sources.financials: SYY_Metrics.csv annual rows (FY2021-FY2026); FY2026 10-K; Q1 FY2027 10-Q (balance sheet 2026-09-26, cover share count 2026-10-16, Notes 8 and 15 for the acquisition financing); Q1 FY2027 and Q4 FY2026 earnings releases (guidance, net debt 10,649, 2.4x leverage); Form 8-K filed 2026-09-14 Exhibits 99.1-99.5 (JRD audited statements, JRD MD&A, unaudited pro forma combined statements); announcement press release 2026-03-30 (JRD ~$16bn revenue, ~$2.1bn EBITDA, $250m synergies, 2.75x long-term leverage target)

inputs.share_count_basis: PRO FORMA for the pending Jetro Restaurant Depot (JRD) acquisition: 492.27m common shares outstanding at 2026-10-16 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q cover; already includes the 12.35m shares sold at $81.00 on 2026-09-16) + ~1.6m dilutive effect of awards (Q1 FY2027 diluted less basic weighted average) + 91.5m Sysco Holdings shares issuable to JRD equity holders at closing = 585.4m. Ties to the 584.3m pro forma diluted count in the 2026-09-14 8-K Exhibit 99.3. Held FLAT thereafter because SBC is expensed in the flows; the 91.5m is genuine non-SBC acquisition currency and is counted up front rather than as share growth.
inputs.net_debt_note: Reported balance sheet at 2026-09-26: current maturities 960 + long-term debt 12,860 (finance leases included) less cash 3,171 = 10,649, the company's own net-debt figure in the Q1 FY2027 release. Cash already holds the $967m equity raise and the C$1.5bn notes. The JRD closing outflows are NOT in these three fields; they are deducted in equity_bridge, taking effective pro forma net debt to ~32.6bn. Junior subordinated notes ($3.9bn USD + EUR 1.0bn, issued 2026-10-06) are treated as 100% debt, no hybrid equity credit.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back (share-based compensation expense $118m; adjusted-EBITDA footnote confirms adjusted EBITDA does NOT exclude it). Cash taxes on net-share settlement are not separately disclosed after FY2018 (~$20-25m/yr then); the forward 0.14%-of-sales path is held flat rather than declining to cover them.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest 30 June (FY2026 ended 2026-06-27; FY2027 is a 53-week year ending 2027-07-03)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.5% (10y UST; Sysco's own 10-year senior notes priced at 5.95% on 2026-10-06), ERP 5%, relevered beta ~0.85 -> cost of equity ~8.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.7% on the new 5.45-7.35% coupons. At the post-close capital structure (~42% debt) that is ~7.1%; at the 2.75x target leverage (~30% debt) ~7.6%. 8.0% used for all three scenarios, a modest margin over the build. No per-scenario WACC differences and no ad-hoc premium: leverage, integration and antitrust risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, so operating lease liabilities (~1.5bn Sysco, ~0.3bn JRD) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases sit inside reported debt and stay there; the non-cash finance-lease fleet additions (55m FY2026, 202m FY2025) are covered by setting the capex path ~0.1pt of sales above guided cash capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial; no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company; adaptations file read for leases and working-capital sign). First valuation of this ticker. BASIS: PRO FORMA for the pending ~$29.1bn JRD acquisition (merger agreement 2026-03-30; $21.6bn cash + 91.5m shares; expected to close by fiscal Q3 FY2027, subject to HSR clearance). Financing is complete (equity 2026-09-16; C$1.5bn, $10.75bn senior, $3.9bn + EUR 1.0bn junior subordinated notes Sept/Oct 2026; bridge terminated 2026-10-08), so a standalone model would be valuing a company that no longer exists on this balance sheet. JRD figures are from the 2026-09-14 8-K (Ex. 99.1-99.5: audited JRD statements, JRD MD&A, pro forma combined statements): JRD LTM-June-2026 sales 16,008, operating income 2,073 (12.9%), EBITDA ~2.2bn (~14%), capex ~137m; pro forma combined FY2026 sales 100,561. REVENUE PATH is on the reported basis, so years 1-2 carry the acquisition step: FY2027 = Sysco +6% on a 53-week basis (company guidance is STANDALONE and 53-week; it does not include JRD) plus ~4.5 months of JRD; FY2028 = 52-week Sysco plus a full JRD year. EBITDA margin path is pre-SBC and AFTER a recurring haircut for 'Certain Items': Sysco's adjusted operating income has exceeded GAAP by 300-360m of cash restructuring/transformation cost every recent year, so the path sits ~0.15-0.4pt below the company-adjusted figure (largest in FY2027-28 for integration). D&A path (1.15%) is the tax-relevant figure: it excludes the ~626m/yr amortisation of acquired JRD intangibles, which arises in a stock merger and is not tax-deductible. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor, growth consumes cash (Sysco NWC ~5.4% of sales; JRD runs negative NWC). Capture set to -2.5% rather than the ~-4.5% organic marginal rate because the engine applies it to the acquisition-driven revenue steps in years 1-2 as well; -2.5% over-charges those two years and under-charges later years by roughly offsetting present values. BUYBACKS are paused (only 200m in FY2026) until deleveraging progresses, so the flat count is a modelling convention not currently being funded; SBC is 0.14% of sales so the effect is trivial. Interest income not stripped: the company is a net debtor and the pre-close interest on invested financing proceeds is handled in the bridge. PRICE: regular-session close; price refresh runs separately. NOT MODELLED: a deal-break branch. If HSR clearance fails Sysco owes a 1.164bn termination fee and the acquisition notes (except the 2036 series) are mandatorily redeemed at 101; the stock fell ~13-16% on announcement, so a break is not obviously value-destructive, but it is not the central case.

base.growth_note: Y1 FY2027: Sysco 84,553 x 1.06 (low end of 6-7% guide, 53 weeks) = ~89.6bn plus ~4.5 months of JRD at a ~16.5bn run-rate (~6.2bn) = ~95.8bn. Y2 FY2028: Sysco on 52 weeks +3.5% (~91.0bn) plus a full JRD year (~17.0bn) = ~108bn. Thereafter organic 3.5% fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_note: Pro forma FY2026 adjusted EBITDA before SBC is ~6.7% of combined sales (Sysco 4,387 + 118 SBC; JRD ~2,240). Path adds the $250m synergy target phased over three years (~0.2pt) and deducts recurring Certain Items: ~500m in FY2027, ~400m in FY2028, ~300m in FY2029, ~0.15pt of sales thereafter. Mature 6.8%.
base.tax_note: Blend of Sysco's ~23-24% effective rate and JRD's ~28%; FY2027 slightly lower on bonus depreciation and ~$300m of purchased transferable tax credits.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0%/2.5% implies 18.6x terminal FCF; the 16x cap binds (about 10x terminal EBITDA, below Sysco's own trading history and the ~14x EBITDA paid for JRD).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: post-close leverage of ~4.5x on a ~4%-FCF-margin business, an unproven transformational integration into a retail format Sysco has not run, and open antitrust risk (the FTC blocked Sysco/US Foods in 2015). Base 50%: guidance was reaffirmed, financing is locked at fixed coupons and both businesses have long records of stable cash generation. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs above-market organic growth, margin expansion and over-delivered synergies together, and Sysco's own adjusted EBITDA margin has been flat for three years.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
